static_traits.name: Wang Yu
static_traits.family_status: Both parents are military personnel, no siblings
static_traits.social_status: Keeping in touch with girlfriend (living in Salt Lake City) but not yet sharing specific Anxiety; Increased stress when comparing with other dog owners; relationship with pets affected by Anxiety
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past psychotherapy experience; has not previously had similar Anxiety or pet training problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, fairly cooperative; able to identify and describe automatic thoughts and negative comparisons; neutral tone, but tends to focus on negatives and overlook positive progress

basic_info.main_problem: Strong Fear and Anxiety because two beagles (Chance and Boomer) cannot learn the 'heel' command; Increasing stress after comparing with others, avoiding training and feeling guilty, affecting daily life and the relationship with the pets.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to ease the overwhelming Anxiety and Fear related to dog training, gaining counseling support to Recovery daily life and physical-mental state.
growth_experiences: Family-of-origin background: both parents are military personnel, no siblings. Has not previously had similar Anxiety or pet training problems, has not yet received psychotherapy, physically healthy with no major illness.

core_beliefs: I am an incompetent owner / I am not good enough
If I cannot meet others' or the standards' Demands, I am just a failure

special_situations.event: With other dog owners, seeing their dogs are better trained
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my dog training is not as good as others', it shows I am incompetent, I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids training scenes and socializing to avoid being compared and evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Others will think I am incompetent; my dogs will never learn heel

special_situations.event: Reading training tips and success stories online
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not met the online standards, it proves I did not do well enough; I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly searching for more techniques but stopping training under Anxiety, ignoring existing progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They still cannot learn; I did not do well enough

special_situations.event: During actual training, the dog responds poorly to the heel command
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is no immediate improvement now, there will be no progress in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding training to escape feelings of failure and Anxiety

special_situations.event: Thinking of how others will view oneself and the dog's training
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am seen as not good enough, it proves I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hiding the problem, not asking the girlfriend or others for help
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They look down on me / think I did not do well enough

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and accepted, affirmed as a competent pet owner
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as a failure, feeling shame and loss of control (the dog not obeying, training ineffective)
defense_goal: Lowers the sense of being judged and failing by avoiding training and socializing
Maintains a fragile sense of self-esteem safety through self-blame and high standards

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent owner prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Picky others / better dog owners who compare and judge
A pet hard to control with poor responsiveness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to compare dog training results in front of others or with others, or thinking of others' evaluations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that others will see them as a failed pet owner (transference: casting inner self-criticism toward the outside)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tends to use generalized statements like 'they will all think...', with an uneasy tone, avoiding specific evidence; in counseling, evidence can be gently probed to help distinguish facts from speculation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to share troubles with the girlfriend or others and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing others' value of 'solving problems alone' as self-Demands, seeing asking for help as weakness or troubling others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses self-Demands language containing 'should/must', in a restrained tone; in counseling, invite them in a supportive tone to identify the source of 'should' and encourage trying limited help-seeking.

manifestations: Unwilling to share specific Anxiety with the girlfriend, tending to bear problems alone
Self-isolates due to comparison in training and social situations
outcomes: Avoiding training, Relationship tension (with the pet)

manifestations: Takes 'should / must solve it alone' as a self-rule, limiting choices and help-seeking
Makes decisions within the framework of others' evaluations (external standards)
outcomes: Behavioral Restricted choices, stuck in avoidance and helplessness

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using language like 'I should/must solve it myself'
Uses others' or online standards as the yardstick for self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Restrains the urge to seek support, turning to self-blame and guilt
When frustrated in training, turns energy into criticism of oneself rather than external communication or adjusting the plan

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Caring excessively about others' evaluations and comparisons
Measuring training success or failure by all-or-nothing standards, belittling or ignoring positive progress

exception_events.target_problem: When training the dog's heel command, the client usually develops intense Anxiety from catastrophizing and comparison, avoiding training and interrupting practice.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In most off-leash situations, both dogs performed well, and executed some commands better than before; the client thus realized it is 'not entirely impossible', with a more balanced view of training.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding and focus: noticing specific progress and shifting the standard from 'instant perfection' to 'gradual improvement'; task breakdown: focusing on reinforcing mastered commands rather than constant comparison; thereby reducing Anxiety and increasing the sense of control.

positive_force: Has begun seeking counseling, willing to practice decatastrophizing and setting small goals
Able to identify and acknowledge the dog's progress on some commands and in off-leash situations
Has potential support resources (staying in touch with the girlfriend)
Willing to try behavioral experiments and gradual goals
negative_force: Catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking, excessive comparison and mind reading
Avoiding training leads to less experience and positive feedback
Strong tendency toward external validation, easily evaluates oneself by others' standards
Shame and guilt intensify, hindering help-seeking and continued practice

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids and interrupts the dog's following (heel) training
antecedent: The dog responds poorly to the heel command during training
Interacting with other dog owners and seeing others train better
Reads training tips and success cases online and compares
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and negative predictions about the future ('they will never learn'), all-or-nothing standards and excessive comparison triggering shame and fear of being judged.
target_behavior.function: Escaping feelings of failure and being judged, briefly reducing Anxiety and guilt
target_behavior.consequence: Training progress blocked, Relationship tension with the pet, daily life and activities affected, Anxiety maintained and worsened
